title: Freeze source truth, support matrix, and behavioral baseline
intent: Convert authoring-time assumptions into an execution-ready inventory without losing prior work.
steps: Read the preserved conversation and source manifest.
Inspect current AGENTS.md and owner instructions.
Inspect related plan phase evidence and last activity.
Record current commits and relevant dirty paths.
Inventory available Bridge nodes and emulator targets through owner APIs.
Identify actual desktop user sessions on candidate hosts.
Freeze exact primary OS, architecture, compositor, and package rows.
Capture the Plan Manager baseline collection through its producer command.
Wait once through the producer and sync the baseline receipt.
Record missing authority separately from repairable environment friction.
Publish the support matrix with pending evidence cells.
checks: Inspect baseline coverage for every captured member.
Check source snapshot hashes against the source manifest.
Use owner status commands for available test hosts.
gates: Every primary support row has an explicit target or an unresolved access request.
Baseline coverage is complete before it is used as the regression oracle.
No historical plan status is treated as current implementation proof.
risk: Newly unavailable hosts do not justify skipping platform implementation.

title: Declare product targets, requirements, and ownership contracts
intent: Create falsifiable obligations before implementation expands across owners.
steps: Read owner PRDs and current requirement IDs.
Add operational targets for surface parity and native companion behavior.
Add desktop session, control, streaming, and recovery requirements.
Add optional-provider and package-profile requirements.
Assign each invariant to one enforcing owner.
Link proposed acceptance cases to requirement IDs.
Update DOMAINS.md and architecture zone maps.
Declare artifact retention and privacy obligations.
Record commercial claims separately from tested capability.
Keep unearned requirements in progress.
checks: Run owner requirement validation and PRD lint.
Inspect each requirement for one falsifiable behavior.
Check every mandatory corpus case has an owner.
gates: No critical behavior exists only in plan prose.
Every new requirement has a planned producer test and a unique owner.
Required platform claims remain unearned until live evidence exists.

title: Extend shared target and surface reference contracts
intent: Give all consumers one safe identity vocabulary without creating another inventory database.
steps: Inspect api-core targetmodel and current proto projections.
Separate target, surface, and session identities.
Preserve Bridge attached-device host relationships.
Define safe owner-scoped surface descriptors.
Add readiness reason conversion without collapsing unknown into absent.
Represent desktop session and display identities explicitly.
Define protocol-version negotiation fields.
Regenerate affected Go and TypeScript clients.
Update existing projections through shared converters.
Add round-trip and malformed-reference tests.
checks: Run targetmodel package tests.
Run affected owner contract suites.
Round-trip descriptors through Go and TypeScript serialization.
gates: Identical owner targets retain identity across Portal and Web Console.
Credentials and transport endpoints never appear in safe descriptors.
Terminal dispatchability is not used as desktop readiness.

title: Implement federated catalog and provider readiness
intent: Make target discovery fast, explicit, and resilient to optional source failure.
steps: Extend Portal integrations with lazy provider adapters.
Aggregate owner surface descriptors within a fixed deadline.
Reuse Web Console catalog semantics where applicable.
Expose partial-source status without deleting healthy targets.
Cache observations with timestamps and explicit stale state.
Reject ambiguous user target selection.
Join device transports by owner identity.
Distinguish companion host from API host.
Add typed recovery actions referencing existing owners.
Preserve favorites separately from authoritative inventory.
outputs: Portal surface catalog API and CLI
checks: Inject absent, slow, malformed, and unauthorized provider responses.
Run Portal and Web Console catalog suites.
Verify a remote API host does not become This machine.
gates: Portal boots and returns healthy sources when another provider is absent.
Ambiguous target names require resolution before side effects.
Readiness facts retain source, time, and reason.

title: Build desktop user-session registry and helper protocol
intent: Establish the authenticated native boundary shared by manual and automated control.
steps: Enumerate desktop sessions through OS-specific discovery seams.
Define helper registration and protocol negotiation.
Bind helper identity to the actual OS user session.
Implement authenticated local IPC with bounded messages.
Expose permission and capability probes independently.
Store session metadata behind a repository interface.
Add helper heartbeat and stale-registration handling.
Separate observation sessions from control leases.
Add native helper lifecycle through existing setup owners.
Document session selection and unavailable reasons.
checks: Test forged helper identity and wrong-user IPC requests.
Test absent display, locked session, and stale heartbeat.
Run Device Control session and contract suites.
gates: An available API cannot masquerade as an available desktop.
Only authenticated helpers register for their user session.
Unsupported and denied capabilities remain distinguishable.

title: Implement destination authority, control epochs, and receipts
intent: Prevent wrong-target input, competing controllers, and duplicate effects.
steps: Bind grants to actor, target, user session, effects, and expiry.
Share the control lease between manual input and flows.
Add control epochs and reject prior holders.
Persist command admission and outcome receipts.
Define duplicate identity and conflicting-payload responses.
Release held keys and buttons on stop.
Reconcile uncertain native effects after helper interruption.
Expire authority after disconnected lease loss.
Record audit references without private input bodies.
Add an independent local emergency-stop path.
checks: Exercise simultaneous controllers and stale epochs.
Interrupt after admission, native effect, and receipt persistence.
Assert held-input release and replay refusal.
gates: Wrong-target or expired input produces no native action.
Duplicate requests never blindly repeat uncertain side effects.
Local stop invalidates queued control despite remote disconnect.

title: Build the cross-platform desktop acceptance fixture
intent: Create a repeatable test application that measures real semantic and visual control.
steps: Create an isolated fixture app with semantic controls and a visual-only canvas.
Include text input, menus, dialogs, export, scrolling, drag, and multiple windows.
Provide deterministic outcome files and independent assertions.
Support localization, DPI, display rearrangement, and layout variants.
Add a reset command through the fixture owner.
Use test-routed storage and unique run namespaces.
Package the fixture for every primary platform.
Add permission-denied and cancellation journeys.
Publish machine-readable case identifiers.
Keep private customer applications outside automated acceptance.
checks: Run fixture self-tests and packaging checks.
Verify independent assertions fail on deliberately wrong outcomes.
Inspect test storage isolation.
gates: The fixture distinguishes delivered input from achieved outcomes.
All primary platforms can run the same behavioral specification.
Fixture resets preserve unrelated machine state.

title: Implement Windows desktop adapter
intent: Deliver real Windows semantic observation, capture, and input in the intended user session.
steps: Evaluate direct UI Automation and Terminator against the fixture.
Record dependency, license, helper language, and packaging decision.
Implement window and element enumeration.
Implement element invocation and value-setting where supported.
Implement screenshot capture and display geometry.
Implement keyboard, Unicode text, pointer, wheel, and drag actions.
Report inaccessible or elevated surfaces explicitly.
Reconnect helper registration after user-session changes.
Bind observations and actions to session identity.
Validate the signed-helper path when credentials are available.
checks: Run the native fixture on Windows x64.
Test session isolation, elevation boundary, IME, and display scaling.
Run Device Control strategy conformance.
gates: Windows primary fixture cases pass through real native APIs.
Executable presence alone never yields ready status.
Unsupported protected surfaces return explicit refusal without false success.
risk: UI Automation visibility varies by application and privilege level.

title: Implement macOS desktop adapter
intent: Deliver permission-aware macOS desktop control with stable signed application identity.
steps: Implement Accessibility-based windows and element resolution.
Implement ScreenCaptureKit capture behind a helper seam.
Implement native input and text actions.
Bind helper registration to the logged-in user session.
Probe capture permission through an actual operation.
Expose Accessibility and Screen Recording recovery instructions.
Preserve signing identity across helper updates.
Handle display scale, multiple screens, and focus changes.
Release input and invalidate epochs on helper restart.
Validate refusal on locked or unauthorized sessions.
checks: Run the fixture on macOS arm64.
Test grant, deny, revoke, restart, and update journeys.
Run capture/input geometry and strategy conformance.
gates: macOS primary semantic, input, and capture cases pass.
Permission revocation immediately removes usable authority.
Helper updates preserve the documented permission behavior.

title: Implement Linux X11 and Wayland desktop adapters
intent: Deliver explicitly supported Linux backends without hiding compositor differences.
steps: Retain X11 as a named backend while replacing weak readiness probes.
Implement AT-SPI semantic observation and actions.
Implement X11 capture and complete input support.
Implement portal-based Wayland capture and authorized input.
Evaluate libei through governed dependency selection.
Declare GNOME and KDE backend capabilities separately.
Report missing portal interfaces as unsupported or unavailable.
Handle portal session revocation and reconnect.
Validate scale, display origin, keyboard layout, and Unicode.
Prevent fallback to X11 when the active Wayland session is incompatible.
checks: Run the fixture on X11, GNOME Wayland, and KDE Wayland.
Test portal grant denial and session revocation.
Run strategy conformance for each backend.
gates: Each required Linux environment passes its declared interaction cases.
No backend advertises capability from PATH checks alone.
Unavailable Wayland access cannot trigger uncontrolled shell fallback.

title: Implement semantic resolution and observation geometry
intent: Make desktop references survive movement while refusing ambiguous or stale actions.
steps: Extend selectors with application and window constraints.
Use existing semantic resolver interfaces where possible.
Return zero, unique, or ambiguous match dispositions.
Attach capture geometry and observation revision to results.
Resolve pointer context before companion focus changes.
Implement bounded crops and annotated-region references.
Revalidate geometry before coordinate actions.
Use event-driven waits with bounded fallback polling.
Add per-adapter semantic capability details.
Retain independent postcondition checks.
checks: Run multi-window, renamed-control, zero-match, and duplicate-label cases.
Move windows and change DPI between observe and act.
Test annotations through scale and crop transformations.
gates: An old coordinate cannot silently target a different control.
Multiple matches never become automatic lowest-ID selection.
Context references preserve the original source and geometry.

title: Extend Bridge with typed desktop session transport
intent: Carry authorized desktop sessions remotely while preserving terminal behavior.
steps: Inspect current interactive frame and admission implementations.
Add typed session-kind negotiation without overloading terminal fields.
Bind remote offers to node, user session, protocol, and authority.
Reuse sequencing, flow-control, and lifetime machinery.
Carry control receipts and explicit outcome-unknown states.
Reconnect using existing durable session identities.
Reject protocol confusion and arbitrary command payloads.
Close active sessions on node revocation.
Keep attached-device topology linked to the host node.
Preserve terminal resizing and byte-stream behavior.
checks: Run Bridge session and Web Console terminal suites.
Inject channel loss before and after native actuation.
Attempt terminal frames against desktop sessions and vice versa.
gates: Remote desktop actions use the same target-side rules as local actions.
Node revocation terminates existing control authority.
Terminal workflows retain their prior verified behavior.

title: Select and implement screen streaming transport
intent: Deliver interactive viewing with explicit media lifecycle and bounded resource use.
steps: Benchmark WebRTC against the existing transport using the fixed fixture.
Measure LAN/WAN frame age, CPU, bandwidth, and reconnect behavior.
Record the transport decision and infrastructure cost.
Implement authenticated signaling and short-lived media authorization.
Configure relay deployment through existing owners if selected.
Bound frame queues and discard stale visual frames.
Keep input and stop channels responsive under congestion.
Implement a labeled screenshot fallback.
Close media paths on revocation and expiry.
Expose diagnostics without leaking session credentials.
checks: Run 1080p fixture streaming under declared network profiles.
Test packet loss, slow viewers, relay-only connectivity, and revocation.
Verify input ordering and bounded memory under congestion.
gates: Required LAN/WAN budgets pass on the declared measurement rig.
Revoked viewers lose existing media access.
Screenshot fallback is explicit and does not claim video parity.
risk: TURN or another relay may require infrastructure authority and recurring cost.

title: Implement Portal surfaces and shared target UX
intent: Provide one workspace for machines, devices, scenarios, browsers, and terminals.
steps: Add target hierarchy and capability-aware surface selection.
Reuse catalog components between Portal and Web Console where behavior matches.
Render desktop, terminal, browser, scenario, and screenless-device panels.
Keep target labels visible during control.
Persist layout and favorites as Portal preferences.
Attach selected surfaces to conversations by stable reference.
Add keyboard navigation and focus restoration.
Show source-specific degraded readiness.
Connect manual controls through owner session APIs.
Expose Stop and Take over without a chat round trip.
checks: Run Portal UI and Web Console integration suites.
Exercise all five surface kinds with real owner adapters.
Test keyboard-only navigation and unavailable surfaces.
gates: Opening a surface never changes its execution owner.
Screenless devices remain usable without fake screens.
Portal and Web Console display consistent target identity and readiness.

title: Harden scenario embeds and context exchange
intent: Embed scenarios without leaking native or cross-target authority.
steps: Extend iframe-bridge through a versioned handshake.
Validate origin, sender window, and message schema.
Bind messages to the active surface session.
Add bounded context and shortcut intent messages.
Prevent embedded content from creating grants or native calls.
Constrain navigation and external-link behavior.
Support resize, focus, theme, and lifecycle signals.
Recover embedded surface failures independently from chat.
Redact private fields from context projection.
Document the minimal provider embedding contract.
checks: Inject forged origin, oversized payload, stale session, and native-call requests.
Run iframe-bridge and Portal embedding tests.
Verify a failed iframe leaves chat usable.
gates: Embedded scenarios cannot inherit trusted-shell privileges.
Valid context messages remain bound to the source surface.
Shortcut escalation does not steal input from active controls.

title: Implement capability-aware task planning and fallback
intent: Construct executable tasks that remain honest when optional providers are missing.
steps: Define task capability requirements and route constraints.
Resolve exact target, account, authority, and data policy.
Bound provider discovery and readiness probes.
Validate all required bindings before execution.
Separate absent, stopped, unhealthy, denied, unsupported, and unknown states.
Offer owner-managed setup or recovery actions.
Permit fallback only when constraints and acceptance remain equivalent.
Reconcile original receipts after uncertain side effects.
Persist route decisions and task identity.
Expose typed reasons in UI and CLI.
checks: Run absent-provider and mid-task-loss matrices.
Test account, target, and residency mismatches.
Verify no side effects occur when preflight fails.
gates: Application startup does not depend on optional control providers.
Fallback never changes target or authority silently.
Unknown side effects prevent blind retry through another provider.

title: Extend desktop flows and verified replay
intent: Use existing flow ownership for desktop tasks and preserve acceptance during repair.
steps: Extend Device Control steps for native semantic and complete input actions.
Add application/session compatibility constraints.
Parameterize reusable task inputs.
Retain durable version and source-run identity.
Require terminal outcome assertions.
Run candidates in isolated test contexts.
Verify replay before promotion.
Preserve assertions and approved effects during repair.
Retain exact old versions for replay.
Expose flow references through Portal without copying flow state.
checks: Run existing BAS and Device Control promotion regressions.
Test failed, incomplete, dry-run, stale-version, and weakened-assertion candidates.
Replay an old version after a newer version is promoted.
gates: Only verified candidates become reusable flows.
Repair cannot weaken the original acceptance contract.
One flow version executes identically through CLI and Portal.

title: Implement bounded vision control and demonstration authoring
intent: Convert unfamiliar desktop interaction into inspectable candidates without unbounded exploration.
steps: Add selected model/provider configuration through existing AI owners.
Provide bounded screenshots and semantic observations.
Enforce action, inference, time, and retry budgets.
Record proposed actions and outcome evidence.
Add demonstration capture with explicit start and stop.
Convert demonstrations into semantic selectors where possible.
Mark visual-only steps with compatibility constraints.
Route generated code through governed bindings.
Reject instruction-like screen content that expands authority.
Produce a candidate rather than silently promoting exploration.
checks: Run recorded vision fixtures before live model smoke.
Execute the fixed adaptive holdout corpus with budgets.
Test malicious on-screen instructions and exhausted budgets.
gates: Every live agent run terminates within declared budgets.
Exploration cannot expand grants or change the requested target.
Promoted results still pass independent outcome assertions.

title: Author Portal programs and scenario skill sets
intent: Make the new capabilities discoverable and reusable by fresh agents.
steps: Read skill-set-authoring, program-runtime, and skill-validation.
Inventory repeated workflows and existing bindings.
Create Portal usage and improvement skills.
Extend Device Control usage guidance for desktop sessions.
Author only programs that own recurring bounded composition.
Declare effects, budgets, fixtures, and failure envelopes.
Register skills and programs beside their scenarios.
Run divergence probes for routing decisions.
Retire procedural prose replaced by typed operations.
Capture outcomes through the existing Memory learning contract.
checks: Run skill-set and programs phases for each changed owner.
Explain every program through Program Runtime.
Run negative binding, budget, and provider-absence fixtures.
gates: A fresh agent chooses the same route for the same observed state.
Programs cannot invoke undeclared control bindings.
Skills direct real operation and measurement rather than hand-authored success claims.

title: Add governed native extension support to Scenario-to-Desktop
intent: Package native Portal features without forking the vanilla Electron template.
steps: Define a versioned extension schema and compatibility policy.
Add approved native module and entrypoint declarations.
Validate feature permissions and target support.
Generate hooks from declared configuration.
Keep trusted shell and untrusted renderer paths separate.
Package native helpers and their metadata.
Integrate signing and update artifacts.
Reject arbitrary template mutation and undeclared native imports.
Add vanilla-consumer regression fixtures.
Document extension authoring and regeneration.
checks: Generate vanilla and companion fixtures from clean inputs.
Test invalid extension versions and undeclared privileges.
Build each primary target through the ramp.
gates: Portal native features are expressed through the extension contract.
A vanilla consumer remains functional after regeneration.
Unsupported extension combinations fail before packaging.

title: Build Portal pill, palette, and full-UI companion
intent: Deliver one conversation experience with native activation and compact states.
steps: Create Portal desktop extension configuration.
Mount normal Portal UI in expanded mode.
Reuse chat and target state in compact modes.
Implement global shortcut with conflict diagnostics.
Implement tray/menu-bar actions and configurable background behavior.
Implement pill and palette positioning.
Capture active context before focusing the palette.
Restore prior focus on dismissal where supported.
Persist conversation, branch, attachments, and run identity across transitions.
Implement explicit quit and running-task disposition.
checks: Run hidden/pill/palette/expanded transitions with an active task.
Test API host different from companion host.
Test shortcut conflicts, display removal, restart, and keyboard-only use.
gates: Expanded companion is the normal Portal UI implementation.
Mode changes preserve conversation and task identity.
This machine resolves to the actual companion host.

title: Implement context selection, annotation, and native privacy UX
intent: Make pointing and drawing useful without misidentifying or oversharing context.
steps: Capture window, pointer, and available selected text before activation.
Add region selection and annotation overlays.
Store original image and transforms as bounded artifact references.
Preview attached context before model submission.
Support explicit context removal and recapture.
Exclude protected fields where platform APIs support it.
Define retention and cleanup policy for capture artifacts.
Revalidate target references before acting.
Preserve context across compact and expanded views.
Expose unavailable capture capabilities without blocking text chat.
checks: Test negative display origins, rotated displays, scaling, and moved windows.
Test revoked capture permission and expired artifact access.
Verify context preview matches submitted source references.
gates: Annotations remain attached to the intended source geometry.
Old screenshots cannot silently authorize new coordinates.
Text chat remains usable when native context capture is unavailable.

title: Integrate optional speech input and output
intent: Add voice interaction through Audio Tools without creating another audio engine.
steps: Inspect Audio Tools STT/TTS session contracts.
Integrate microphone lifecycle with explicit user activation.
Support partial transcript display and cancellation.
Route speech output through the owner playback interface.
Preserve typed chat when audio is absent or denied.
Prevent duplicate submission after reconnect or transcript finalization.
Expose device selection and permission recovery.
Keep capture privacy and retention consistent with context policy.
Separate audio timing from task execution timing.
Validate voice in compact and expanded modes.
checks: Run Audio Tools and Portal integration suites.
Test denied microphone, missing provider, cancellation, and duplicate final events.
Run one live STT and TTS journey per supported native environment.
gates: Voice uses existing Audio Tools ownership.
Missing audio never prevents text interaction.
One utterance produces at most one submitted task.

title: Implement optional deployment profiles and setup recovery
intent: Make packaged Portal usable with local, remote, or absent optional providers.
steps: Map profile intent into existing dependency and bundle contracts.
Implement client, local-control, and automation profiles.
Resolve required providers from bundle or configured endpoint.
Keep optional providers out of fatal startup dependencies.
Expose feature availability before task submission.
Route installation and lifecycle repair through existing owners.
Verify fresh-machine path and credential discovery.
Persist endpoint selections without leaking secrets.
Test offline startup and later provider attachment.
Document package size and capability differences.
checks: Install each profile in a clean environment.
Remove BAS, Device Control, Audio Tools, and Program Runtime independently.
Test configured remote providers and expired credentials.
gates: Client profile opens without control providers.
Required profile capabilities are verified or explicitly fail setup.
Optional setup never triggers an unauthorized purchase or install.

title: Validate remote machines, attached devices, and compute targets
intent: Prove the unified target model across real fleet topologies.
steps: Use existing Bridge enrollment for available authorized hosts.
Expose remote desktops and terminals through their owners.
Join an attached phone or TV with its Bridge host.
Render a screenless device as a capability panel.
Inspect compute-managed nodes without assuming a GUI.
Offer owner-managed desktop provisioning only with authority.
Run a local-to-remote cross-capability task.
Retain destination labels in every task and result.
Test node revoke and attached-device revoke independently.
Verify no cross-node account substitution during fallback.
checks: Run desktop and terminal tasks on remote primary hosts.
Exercise one attached device and one screenless fixture.
Test remote host offline, revoked, and terminal-only states.
gates: Machine and attached-device identities remain distinct and linked.
A terminal-only compute node never advertises a desktop.
Remote control honors the same verification and authority as local control.

title: Implement learning sensors and comparable performance benchmarks
intent: Measure the agent-effort improvement that motivated the work.
steps: Instrument orientation, discovery, route selection, first action, and verified completion.
Record tool round trips and visual reasoning calls when observed.
Separate cold/warm and local/remote cohorts.
Capture reuse and failure fingerprints through Memory.
Define golden corpora and independent success checks.
Run paired fresh-authoring and saved-replay benchmarks.
Compute quantiles with explicit denominators.
Expose typed setpoint sensors and unavailable reasons.
Test improvement routing without weakening floors.
Publish reproducible benchmark commands and raw references.
checks: Run the declared 50/30/20-pair sample budgets.
Verify missing observations remain absent.
Compare equal task outcomes and capture practices.
gates: All stated latency budgets have measured pass/fail evidence.
Reused-task effort meets the declared reduction on the fixed corpus.
Operator-learning claims are separate from synthetic benchmark evidence.

title: Migrate old Assistant capture and retire duplicate runtime
intent: Preserve useful behavior and history while removing redundant ownership.
steps: Inventory old Assistant runtime, commands, data, and integrations.
Export useful history with stable identifiers and checksums.
Implement Portal issue capture through current reporting owners.
Link captured context to the resulting task or issue.
Reconcile migrated record counts and relationships.
Validate keyboard capture and agent handoff replacement.
Retain original data until migration review permits removal.
Remove redundant runtime wiring after replacement acceptance.
Update discoverability and operator documentation.
Record any intentionally unsupported old behavior with rationale.
checks: Run migration against a representative copy of old data.
Exercise hotkey capture through new Portal UX.
Verify unrelated original data remains unchanged.
gates: Useful history survives migration without duplicate task creation.
Issue capture uses current owners and verified context.
No second desktop-control or conversation engine remains active.

title: Complete security, isolation, and interruption validation
intent: Prove the privilege and temporal boundaries under hostile and interrupted inputs.
steps: Run hostile iframe and renderer messages.
Run forged target, helper, session, and grant identities.
Inject malicious instructions into captured app content.
Interrupt helper, API, Bridge, and media processes at defined boundaries.
Test expired and revoked artifact access.
Test out-of-order, duplicate, and oversized input messages.
Test control takeover while keys and buttons are held.
Test program budget exhaustion and sandbox escape attempts.
Inspect logs and diagnostics for secrets.
Repair every critical boundary failure before release validation.
checks: Execute every mandatory security corpus case.
Run owner security and regression suites.
Inspect actual target-side effects after rejected requests.
gates: Unauthorized requests produce no forbidden effects.
Interrupted runs preserve honest outcome state and release control.
Native privileges remain isolated from scenario embeds and generated content.

title: Validate native installation, updates, and recovery across platforms
intent: Prove the delivered bytes and their lifecycle on supported machines.
steps: Build release candidates with pinned inputs and dependency evidence.
Install on clean primary platform hosts.
Verify first-run permissions and provider profiles.
Test update from a representative predecessor.
Verify helper signing identity and protocol compatibility.
Test interrupted update and restart recovery.
Test launch at login only when enabled.
Test explicit quit and uninstall cleanup.
Preserve retained user data according to the selected policy.
Link artifact digests to tested-byte receipts.
checks: Run ramp-owned platform validation through Bridge hosts.
Verify artifact digest equality across build, test, and candidate records.
Run deployment readiness review for the exact candidate.
gates: Every primary package row has real lifecycle evidence.
Tested bytes equal release-candidate bytes.
Missing production signing evidence remains an explicit unresolved release gate.

title: Prepare commercial package and operator documentation
intent: Make the supported product understandable and its claims evidence-backed.
steps: Document the three representative customer journeys.
Produce screenshots or recordings from actual validated runs.
Publish capability and platform support matrices.
Write installation, permission, recovery, privacy, and troubleshooting guides.
Model inference and relay costs with measured inputs.
Draft personal and team packaging hypotheses.
Map marketing claims to acceptance receipts.
Prepare usability study scripts and capture available internal results.
Record missing external customer evidence honestly.
Prepare reviewable launch material without publishing externally.
checks: Walk the installation and recovery guide on a clean host.
Check every capability claim against a support row.
Review all demos for private data and unsupported claims.
gates: Commercial claims match tested capability and limitations.
No invented customer validation or speedup appears in launch material.
Operators can diagnose missing providers and permissions without source inspection.

title: Run end-to-end parity, regression, and completion review
intent: Close the plan only when the whole promised experience is independently evidenced.
steps: Run the same saved task through browser Portal, companion, and CLI.
Run native-app, browser-to-desktop, and remote-machine journeys.
Execute all mandatory acceptance cases and support rows.
Run full changed-owner suites through Test Genie.
Wait once through producer-owned commands.
Run the full captured baseline collection comparison without selectors.
Sync Plan Manager validation receipts.
Reconcile requirement evidence and unresolved findings.
Verify artifact index, digests, and reproduction commands.
Request Plan Manager completion only after all plan-level gates pass.
checks: Use each scenario full suite and the producer baseline collection diff.
Run the acceptance ledger verifier from this plan.
Read Plan Manager completion verdict and remaining gates.
gates: All mandatory deliverables and primary support rows have passing attributable receipts.
The captured collection has no unexplained behavioral regressions.
The final completion verdict is evidence-backed, not a narrative declaration.
